course_name_original: Sistemas Productivos, Fabricación Y Métodos De La Calidad (I.Mecánica)
course_name_en: Production Systems, Manufacturing, and Quality Methods (Mechanical Engineering)
prerequisites: No prior requirements, but it is recommended to take it after passing first and second year courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Unit I. Approach to industrial production
Topic 1. Fundamentals of production systems, manufacturing, and quality methods
Topic 2. Mechanical workshops and equipment
Unit II. Design of the production system
Topic 3. Analysis of the productive process flow
Topic 4. Capacity of the manufacturing and assembly plant
Topic 5. Distribution of processes and facilities
Unit III. Production planning and scheduling
Topic 6. Production order planning
Topic 7. Manufacturing resource planning
Topic 8. Synchronized manufacturing
Topic 9. Workshop management
Unit IV. Production support systems
Topic 10. Material handling, transport, and storage
Topic 11. Warehouse management
Topic 12. Stock management
Unit V. Quality in industrial production
Topic 13. Quality and maintenance in production
Topic 14. Quality control
Topic 15. Maintenance management
teaching_methods: Participation and use of asynchronous virtual learning environment tools (forums, recorded video lessons)
assessment_rules: In the ordinary June session, the final grade is calculated as 0.8 * Final Exam Grade + 0.1 * PEC-1 Grade + 0.1 * PEC-2 Grade. The final exam grade required to pass without PEC is 6. There is no minimum exam grade required to sum the PEC. In the extraordinary September session, the evaluation is based solely on the face-to-face exam, which accounts for 100% of the final grade.
